3. Within the elastic limit, a wire can be broken.
4. Without the use of equipment, a wire can be sliced into pieces.
5. After a long period of service, railway tracks and bridges are deemed unsafe.
6. After a long period of usage, spring balances give incorrect readings.
Project Work:
Project 7.1 Measure and compare the modulus of elasticity of different types of wires
commonly available in society.
Hint: Materials you require: Different material wires such as iron, steel, copper, brass,
aluminum, etc; micrometer and Vernier apparatus, suitable weights, clamps and supporter.
Theory: stress = Y (Young’s modulus of elasticity), stress= 𝐹 and strain = 𝑥. The slope of

Procedural idea: i) Different types of wires such as Copper, Aluminum, Steel, Iron, etc. ii) Equal lengths wires are suspended from a rigid support, cross-sectional area of each is determined by measuring diameter, and loads in steps are attached on the free ends. iii) Extension produced is measured with the Vernier apparatus attached. iv) Finally Stress vs Strain plot is obtained and Y is measured. Repeat it with several other wires and finally compare Ys of all which will be helpful to the society.
